title: Human and LLM Biases in Hate Speech Annotations: A Socio-Demographic Analysis of Annotators and Targets

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing hate speech annotation rates between human annotators and persona-prompted LLMs of different age groups toward targets of various ages using confusion matrices to calculate bias intensity and prevalence.
Measuring systematic differences in how annotators and LLM personas label hate speech directed at individuals with specific disabilities (e.g., cognitive, physical, visually impaired).
Evaluating how the education level of human annotators and LLM personas affects their hate speech annotation behavior.
Comparing hate speech labels assigned by human annotators and LLM personas simulated with different political ideologies (e.g., liberal, conservative).
Analyzing differences in hate speech annotations by different gender groups (including transgender and non-binary individuals) toward targets of varying genders.
Measuring the impact of annotator and LLM persona income levels on their propensity to flag or underestimate hate speech.
Evaluating variations in hate speech annotations directed at targets based on origin, such as immigrants, undocumented individuals, and migrant workers.
Comparing the hate speech labeling behavior of different racial groups toward targets of various races using in-group and out-group statistical comparisons.
Measuring relative differences in hate speech annotations among different religious groups toward targets of various religions.
Analyzing how annotators and LLM personas of different sexual orientations label hate speech directed at various sexual orientation groups (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual, straight).
